metadata.title: Paramedical and Mental Health Practice Platform Data Assets
metadata.description: Catalog of the patient, practitioner and access, scheduling and clinical record, declaration, financing and insight, mental health care and e-health, patient environment, and network, platform and operations data assets that power the Health Cloud Initiative labels (HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE, HCI CRS, Uw Zorg Online, Quli, Embloom, Emogy) for 40,000+ healthcare professionals and 4 million+ patients, with AVG (GDPR) special-category health data classification and BSN handling, WGBO 20-year medical file retention, NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 controls, Wegiz and MedMij exchange obligations, GDS801 and zorgprestatiemodel declaration rules, Jeugdwet and Wmo 2015 municipal financing, the Dutch fiscal retention duty of 7 years for invoices and claims, EU and Netherlands data residency, backing stores and team ownership.

rootGroups.name: Patient, Practitioner and Access Data
rootGroups.description: The data that says who is treated, who treats and who may see what across every HCI label: the patient or client profile with BSN and insurance details, the practitioner profile with AGB code and discipline, the logins of professionals, practice staff and citizens, the consents that permit disclosure to quality registers, portals and personal health environments, and the append-only audit trail that NEN 7510 and the WGBO require for every look into a medical file. This is where the AVG special-category obligation is concentrated: 4 million+ patients and 40,000+ professionals are identified here, and access is bound to the treatment relationship.

subGroups.name: Patients and Practitioners
subGroups.description: The two master records every other asset hangs from: the patient or client as the subject of care and the professional as the accountable treating party, both shared between the paramedical EPDs, CRS, the patient environments and the care-network connectors.

assets.name: Patient Profile
assets.description: One person receiving care in a practice or institution on HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE or HCI CRS: name, address, date of birth, BSN (verified through the SBV-Z or Vecozo identity check), contact preferences, insurer and policy number from the last COV check, general practitioner and pharmacy, legal representative for minors and youth-care clients, communication language, portal and PGO link status and the practices that hold a treatment relationship. Mastered per tenant in Patient Dossier and Care Pathways (dosr), read by the agenda, medication management, the patient app and the HIS/AIS connectors, and matched across labels during migration into HCI One. In GGZ the same record carries the youth-care indication holder and the municipality of residence needed for Jeugdwet financing.
assets.businessMeaning: The identity behind every appointment, note, claim and portal message; a wrong BSN or insurer here becomes a rejected declaration, a mis-delivered e-consult or a dossier shown to the wrong practice.
assets.accessScope: practitioners and practice staff of the tenant that holds a treatment relationship; the patient for their own profile through Uw Zorg Online or the CRS client portal; HCI support staff only inside an approved support session that is logged; BSN visible only in the eligibility and declaration modules

interfaces.name: patient-profile api
interfaces.description: Patient search, create and merge, demographic and insurer attributes, GP and pharmacy links, representative and portal status API used by the agenda, dossier, medication management, declaration engine, patient app and the HIS/AIS connectors; BSN returned only to authorised modules.

interfaces.name: patient profile events
interfaces.description: Patient registered, demographics changed, insurer changed after COV, representative added, portal linked, practice relationship ended and patient merged events consumed by the agenda, declarations, the patient environments, the audit log and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: patient identification exchange
interfaces.description: BSN verification requests and answers with SBV-Z or Vecozo, patient demographics inside GDS801 and zorgprestatiemodel claims, and pseudonymised patient identifiers in LDF and Keurmerk extracts.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the treatment relationship and 20 years after the last change to the medical file, in line with the WGBO retention term, or longer when good care requires it; deleted earlier only on a patient's destruction request that the practitioner honours under WGBO article 455; BSN removed with the dossier
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating practice or institution; demographics passed to insurers and municipalities only inside claims, to referrers inside referral letters, to LDF and other registers only pseudonymised under opt-in consent, and to the patient's PGO only under a MedMij authorisation; never shared between tenants or with partners without a processing agreement

assets.name: Practitioner Profile
assets.description: The professional record of a physiotherapist, allied health therapist, GZ-psychologist, psychiatrist, nurse or other care professional on the platform: name, BIG registration number, AGB code (person and practice), discipline and specialisations (KNGF, NVLF, NVD or GGZ professional standard categories used by the zorgprestatiemodel), UZI-pass identifier where applicable, locations and working hours, contract and settlement role within the practice, quality-register memberships and the tenants the person works for. Mastered in Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (iden) because the professional role determines what may be read and signed, and projected into the agenda, treatment plans, referral messaging and declaration engine where the AGB code and profession are mandatory claim attributes.
assets.businessMeaning: The accountable treating party on every note, claim and referral: the AGB code and profession category decide whether a declaration is accepted and which zorgprestatiemodel tariff applies.
assets.accessScope: the practitioner for their own profile; practice owners and application managers for their own tenant; HCI implementation staff during onboarding; AGB and BIG numbers readable by the declaration and referral modules

interfaces.name: practitioner-profile api
interfaces.description: Practitioner lookup by AGB or BIG number, discipline and specialisation attributes, location and working-hour calendars, tenant membership and signing rights API used by the agenda, treatment plans, referral hub, declaration engine and the Zorgverlener App.

interfaces.name: practitioner profile events
interfaces.description: Practitioner onboarded, AGB or BIG changed, specialisation added, location assigned, left tenant and signing right revoked events consumed by the agenda, declarations, the audit log and access reviews.

interfaces.name: practitioner registers
interfaces.description: AGB register lookups with Vektis and BIG register checks used to validate profession and registration status before declarations are released.

governance.retention: kept while the professional holds an account on any tenant and 7 years after the last claim that names the practitioner, because insurers and the NZa may still examine those claims; BIG and AGB references kept with archived claims
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant and HCI; AGB code and profession shared with insurers and municipalities inside claims and with referrers inside referral messages; never listed publicly except on a practice website with the practitioner's consent

subGroups.name: Identity, Consent and Audit
subGroups.description: The logins of professionals and citizens with UZI, DigiD and two-factor authentication, the consent records that permit each disclosure, and the append-only audit trail that NEN 7510 and the WGBO demand for every access to a medical file.

assets.name: User Identity
assets.description: A login on any HCI label, the Zorgverlener App, Uw Zorg Online, Quli or the CRS client portal: e-mail or username, password hash, two-factor settings, UZI-pass or DigiD assertion references for professionals and citizens, device registrations and push tokens, the roles the person holds (practitioner, practice owner, application manager, billing-service operator, HCI support, patient, client, informal carer, partner developer), the tenants and patient environments the login may open, sessions and refresh tokens, terms and privacy-statement acceptances, invitation status and last sign-in. Managed by Identity, Access and Strong Authentication (iden), consumed on every screen of the Zorgverlener Mobile App (mobi) and written into the audit log for every privileged action.
assets.businessMeaning: The gate to 4 million patient environments and tens of thousands of dossiers: correct roles and strong authentication are what NEN 7510 auditors and insurers check first.
assets.accessScope: the user for their own profile and devices; tenant administrators for role management within their tenant; the platform security team for global administration; credentials, secrets and tokens never readable by anyone

interfaces.name: identity and access api
interfaces.description: Authentication (password, two-factor, UZI, DigiD via the MedMij and DigiD brokers), token issuance and refresh, role and tenant-scope lookup, device registration and session revocation API used by every web app, mobile app and partner integration.

interfaces.name: identity events
interfaces.description: User invited, activated, role changed, two-factor enrolled, login failed repeatedly, session revoked and account closed events consumed by the audit log, security monitoring, support tooling and the warehouse.

governance.retention: kept while the account is active; credentials and tokens deleted at closure, the account stub kept 2 years to answer access requests and security investigations, audit references kept with the audit log
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI; DigiD and UZI assertions never stored beyond the reference needed for audit; never shared with partners or between tenants

assets.name: Data Sharing Consent
assets.description: A recorded decision by a patient, client or their representative to permit or refuse a specific disclosure: opt-in for pseudonymised delivery to the Landelijke Database Fysiotherapie and Keurmerk, participation in Qualiview or MediQuest patient surveys, activation of the patient portal and e-health terms, sharing of the dossier with a referrer or another practice, and the processing-agreement acceptance a tenant gives HCI as processor. Each consent carries the purpose, the wording version shown, who recorded it and how (portal, in-practice, written), the effective and withdrawal dates and the assets it covers. Maintained by Audit Log, Consent and Information Security (audt) and read by Quality Data Delivery (qdat) before any extract is produced.
assets.businessMeaning: The permission behind every disclosure that is not a treatment necessity; without a matching consent an LDF extract, a survey invitation or a shared dossier is a breach rather than a service.
assets.accessScope: the patient for their own consents; practitioners and practice staff of the treating tenant; the quality-data and portal modules for evaluation; HCI privacy officers for audit; never editable retroactively

interfaces.name: consent api
interfaces.description: Consent capture, wording-version lookup, evaluation per purpose and patient, withdrawal and consent history API used by the dossier, quality data delivery, the patient environments and survey integrations.

interfaces.name: consent events
interfaces.description: Consent granted, refused, withdrawn, wording version changed and consent expired events consumed by quality data delivery, the patient app, the audit log and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: consent evidence
interfaces.description: Signed consent forms scanned into the document store and consent status columns inside LDF, Keurmerk and survey extracts.

governance.retention: kept as long as the dossier it governs plus the WGBO term, so that any historical disclosure can be matched to the consent in force at that moment; withdrawal recorded, never deleted
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating tenant; consent status shared with quality registers and survey providers only as an inclusion flag; never shared with insurers or partners

assets.name: Audit Log Entry
assets.description: One immutable record of who did what, when, from which context and on whose data: dossier reads and changes with the treatment-relationship justification, note signatures and AI transcription requests, declaration releases and corrections, portal and PGO accesses by patients and carers, exports and prints, consent changes, configuration changes, integration calls to Vecozo, ZorgDomein, MedMij and HIS/AIS systems, support-session logins and security events such as failed authentication bursts. Written by every brick through Audit Log, Consent and Information Security (audt), and specifically by Voice-to-Text and AI Documentation (vtxt) for every audio fragment processed, with hash chaining so that entries cannot be altered.
assets.businessMeaning: The evidence NEN 7510 and the WGBO logging requirement demand: a patient may ask who looked at their file and HCI must answer, and every security incident investigation starts here.
assets.accessScope: the platform security team and tenant application managers for their own tenant; patients for the access report on their own file; write-only for all bricks; entries never editable or deletable before their retention date

interfaces.name: audit log api
interfaces.description: Append entry, query by subject, actor, tenant and period, patient access-report generation and integrity verification API used by every brick, the client portals and the security operations tooling.

interfaces.name: audit and security events
interfaces.description: Suspicious access pattern, break-glass access used, export performed, integration failure burst and integrity check failed events consumed by security monitoring, support tooling and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: audit exports
interfaces.description: Signed audit extracts for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 audits, patient access reports and incident investigations.

governance.retention: access entries on medical files kept at least as long as the WGBO term of the file they concern and no less than the 5 years commonly advised in Dutch healthcare logging guidance based on NEN 7513; security and configuration entries kept 7 years; entries never overwritten
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and the tenant concerned; access reports handed to the patient on request; extracts shared with certification auditors under confidentiality; never shared with partners

rootGroups.name: Scheduling and Clinical Record Data
rootGroups.description: The operational heart of a paramedical practice: the agenda across therapists and locations that FysioRoadmap and SpotOnMedics call the central hub, group lessons and subscriptions, and the medical file itself with treatment episodes, guideline-driven care pathways, clinical notes produced by typing or voice, and measurement instruments and PROMs. Everything in this group is medical data under the WGBO, kept 20 years, and everything here is also the source from which declarations are generated automatically.

subGroups.name: Agenda and Programmes
subGroups.description: Appointments and recurring programmes across practitioners, rooms and locations, synchronised with online booking, the patient app and the Zorgverlener App, and the basis of automatic declaration generation.

assets.name: Appointment
assets.description: One planned or completed contact between a patient and a practitioner: type (intake, treatment, group lesson, video consultation, telephone contact, no-show), practitioner, location and room, start and duration, the treatment episode and care pathway step it belongs to, booking channel (practice, 24/7 online booking, patient app, referral), reminder and confirmation status, waiting-list origin, cancellation reason and the registration status that decides whether it becomes a declaration line. Mastered in Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling (agnd) and written by Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders (obok) and Patient Appointment Self-service (appb), read by the Zorgverlener Mobile App (mobi) and, as anonymous free slots only, by Practice Websites (pweb); every completed appointment is the seed of a GDS801 claim line or zorgprestatiemodel consult.
assets.businessMeaning: The agenda is the central hub of the practice: a completed appointment is both a treatment record and the unit that is declared, so agenda accuracy equals declaration accuracy and revenue.
assets.accessScope: practitioners and front-desk staff of the tenant; the patient for their own appointments through the app or portal; the declaration engine for completed appointments; practice websites see only free slots, never names

interfaces.name: appointment api
interfaces.description: Availability search across practitioners and locations, book, reschedule, cancel, confirm, mark completed or no-show, waiting-list placement and reminder scheduling API used by the agenda, online booking, the patient app, practice websites, the Zorgverlener App and the declaration engine.

interfaces.name: appointment events
interfaces.description: Appointment booked, rescheduled, cancelled, reminder sent, checked in, completed, no-show recorded and registered-for-declaration events consumed by the dossier, the declaration engine, the patient app, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: agenda synchronisation
interfaces.description: Calendar feeds for practitioners, appointment confirmations by e-mail and SMS, and appointment slots exposed to HIS-connected GP practices through the Uw Zorg Online connectors.

governance.retention: kept with the dossier for the WGBO term of 20 years because appointments evidence the treatment history, and 7 years with the claims they generated; online-booking requests that never became an appointment deleted after 12 months
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant; appointment date, type and practitioner shared with insurers inside claims; availability only shared publicly through the practice website and patient app; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Group Programme
assets.description: A recurring lesson, course or subscription that patients join rather than book individually: exercise groups and fall-prevention courses in physiotherapy, dietetics group programmes, GGZ group treatment, running and fitness subscriptions sold by the practice, with schedule, capacity, instructor, location, enrolled participants and their attendance, price model (per session, per period, insured versus self-paid) and the declaration or invoice rule per participant. Mastered in Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions (grpm) alongside the SpotOnMedics group management heritage, and feeding Patient Invoicing and Payments (pinv) for subscription charges and the agenda for lesson slots.
assets.businessMeaning: Groups and subscriptions are the recurring revenue outside insurance and the most fragile part of billing when attendance and pricing are tracked by hand.
assets.accessScope: practitioners and front-desk staff of the tenant; participants for their own enrolment and attendance in the patient app; invoicing for charges

interfaces.name: group-programme api
interfaces.description: Programme catalogue, schedule and capacity, enrolment, attendance registration, subscription period and pricing-rule API used by the agenda, online booking, the patient app and invoicing.

interfaces.name: group programme events
interfaces.description: Programme created, participant enrolled, attendance recorded, subscription renewed or ended and programme cancelled events consumed by the agenda, invoicing, declarations for insured group sessions and dashboards.

governance.retention: enrolment and attendance kept 7 years with the invoices and claims they support; attendance that is part of a treatment episode kept for the WGBO term of that dossier
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant; participant names never shown to other participants except on printed attendance lists the practice controls; group-session claim lines shared with insurers only for insured treatment

subGroups.name: Dossier and Measurement
subGroups.description: The medical file of a paramedical or GGZ patient: the episode that frames a complaint or diagnosis, the care-pathway templates that structure it per discipline and guideline, the notes produced by typing, dictation or AI summarisation, and the measurement instruments and PROMs that show progress.

assets.name: Treatment Episode
assets.description: One treatment trajectory for one complaint or diagnosis: start and end date, referral or direct-access (DTF) screening, indication and diagnosis codes (DCSPH for physiotherapy, discipline codes for speech and occupational therapy, DSM-based main diagnosis group and zorgvraagtypering for GGZ), the chosen care pathway and its steps, the responsible practitioner and co-treaters, treatment goals, chronic-list status and count of treatments against the insurer's limit, the treatment plan for GGZ, prognosis and the closure with outcome. Mastered in Patient Dossier and Care Pathways (dosr), instantiated from templates by Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates (clin), the unit the Declaration Engine (decl) claims against, the frame of Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination (trpl) and the row every Practice BI Dashboard (bidb) counts.
assets.businessMeaning: The clinical and financial unit of care: it decides which guideline applies, how many treatments are covered, which tariff is declared and what the audit trail must reconstruct twenty years later.
assets.accessScope: the treating practitioner and co-treaters of the tenant; practice owners and application managers for supervision within the treatment relationship; the patient for their own episodes through the portal; the declaration engine for claim attributes; pseudonymised in quality extracts and dashboards

interfaces.name: treatment-episode api
interfaces.description: Episode open, diagnosis and indication coding, pathway assignment and step progression, treatment count and chronic-list status, co-treater assignment, closure and outcome API used by the dossier, guideline templates, the declaration engine, treatment plans, dashboards and quality data delivery.

interfaces.name: episode events
interfaces.description: Episode opened, diagnosis coded, pathway step completed, treatment limit approaching, episode closed and outcome recorded events consumed by the declaration engine, dashboards, quality data delivery, e-health programme assignment and the patient app.

interfaces.name: episode extracts
interfaces.description: Treatment reports and end-of-treatment letters to referrers via ZorgDomein or ZorgMail, dossier exports for a patient or a successor practice, and pseudonymised episode records in LDF extracts.

governance.retention: kept 20 years after the last change to the file under the WGBO, or longer when good care requires it; destroyed earlier only on a patient's request honoured by the practitioner; claim attributes kept 7 years with the declarations
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating tenant; diagnosis and treatment codes shared with insurers and municipalities inside claims and with referrers inside reports; pseudonymised episodes shared with LDF, Keurmerk and benchmarks under consent; exposed to the patient's PGO only under a MedMij authorisation

assets.name: Clinical Note
assets.description: A dated entry in the medical file: anamnesis, examination findings, SOEP or discipline-specific structured note, treatment performed, home advice, correspondence summary, multidisciplinary consultation note or GGZ session report, with author, signature time, addenda after signature, the pathway step it fulfils and its origin (typed, template, dictated and transcribed, AI-summarised from audio with the practitioner's confirmation). Mastered in Patient Dossier and Care Pathways (dosr), produced at scale by Voice-to-Text and AI Documentation (vtxt) and SmartAI in CRS, and never altered after signature except through an addendum.
assets.businessMeaning: The clinical content practitioners spend about a working day per week producing: shortening its creation without weakening its evidential value is the platform's central promise.
assets.accessScope: the treating practitioner and co-treaters; supervising practitioners within the tenant under the treatment relationship; the patient for their own notes through the portal where the practice enables it; AI transcription services process audio only inside the EU under a processing agreement and retain nothing

interfaces.name: clinical-note api
interfaces.description: Note create, structured template fill, dictation transcription and AI draft submission, sign, addendum and read-by-episode API used by the dossier, voice-to-text, treatment plans, the patient portal and referral reporting.

interfaces.name: clinical note events
interfaces.description: Note drafted, transcription completed, note signed, addendum added and note shared with patient events consumed by the audit log, care-pathway progression, the patient portal and the warehouse (counts only).

interfaces.name: dictation and note documents
interfaces.description: Audio fragments handed to the transcription service and deleted after confirmation, and note PDFs inside treatment reports, referrer letters and dossier exports.

governance.retention: kept 20 years after the last change to the file under the WGBO; audio deleted immediately after the transcribed note is confirmed; AI drafts not confirmed by the practitioner deleted within 30 days
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating tenant; shared with referrers only as reports the practitioner releases; shown to the patient through portal or PGO under practice settings and MedMij authorisation; note text never enters analytics, only counts and durations

assets.name: Care Pathway Template
assets.description: A discipline-specific, guideline-based structure for a treatment episode: the steps and required fields for intake, screening, examination, diagnosis, treatment plan, evaluation and closure, the measurement instruments to be offered at each step, the note templates and the audit rules that make a dossier pass an insurer or Keurmerk audit, based on KNGF guidelines for physiotherapy, NVLF for speech therapy, Ergotherapie Nederland and NVD standards, FysioRoadmap and HCI One content, and CRS treatment-plan templates for GGZ. Mastered in Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates (clin), versioned per guideline release and customisable per practice, and instantiated into every treatment episode.
assets.businessMeaning: Templates are how guideline compliance and audit-proof records are delivered without typing: coverage of pathways per discipline is a direct measure of HCI One's readiness for each rollout wave.
assets.accessScope: practice owners and application managers of the tenant for customisation; the clinical content team of HCI for the shared library; every practitioner for use

interfaces.name: care-pathway-template api
interfaces.description: Template catalogue per discipline and guideline version, step and field definitions, measurement and note template bindings, practice customisation and version comparison API used by the dossier, measurement instruments, treatment plans and tenant configuration.

interfaces.name: template events
interfaces.description: Template published, guideline version updated, practice customisation saved and template retired events consumed by the dossier, quality data delivery and tenant configuration.

governance.retention: all versions kept indefinitely because a historical episode must be readable against the template version it was created with
governance.sharingPolicy: shared HCI library available to every tenant; practice-specific customisations internal to that tenant; guideline content used under the licences of KNGF and the other professional associations

assets.name: Measurement Result
assets.description: A scored administration of a measurement instrument or patient-reported outcome measure inside a treatment episode: instrument and version (for example PSK, NPRS, QuickDASH, 6MWT in physiotherapy, discipline instruments for speech and dietetics, and ROM instruments such as OQ-45, BSI, HoNOS or SQ-48 in GGZ), the moment in the pathway (baseline, interim, end), raw item answers, computed scores and norm comparison, who administered it (practitioner, patient through the portal or Embloom link) and the consent status for onward delivery. Mastered in Measurement Instruments and PROMs (meas), orchestrated for GGZ by ROM and Questionnaire Orchestration for GGZ (romq), and the core of what Quality Data Delivery (qdat) sends pseudonymised to LDF, Keurmerk and benchmarks.
assets.businessMeaning: Measurements are how therapists show progress to patients and payers and how the practice earns its Keurmerk and contract status; a missing end measurement is a gap in outcomes and in quality points.
assets.accessScope: the treating practitioner and co-treaters; the patient for their own scores through the portal; quality data delivery only under opt-in consent and pseudonymised; the content team for pseudonymised norm calibration

interfaces.name: measurement-result api
interfaces.description: Instrument administration, patient self-administration links, scoring and norm comparison, progress graphs per episode and consent-aware extract API used by the dossier, ROM orchestration, the patient app, dashboards and quality data delivery.

interfaces.name: measurement events
interfaces.description: Measurement requested, patient completed, scored, threshold alert raised, end measurement missing and result shared with patient events consumed by the dossier, treatment plans, quality data delivery and dashboards.

interfaces.name: measurement extracts
interfaces.description: Pseudonymised measurement rows inside monthly LDF and Keurmerk deliveries, benchmark files returned by the registers and questionnaire results imported from Embloom.

governance.retention: kept 20 years with the dossier under the WGBO; pseudonymised copies in the staging zone deleted 90 days after delivery confirmation
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating tenant; pseudonymised results delivered monthly to LDF, Keurmerk and benchmark registers under opt-in consent; individual scores shared with the patient and, on release, with referrers inside reports; never shared with insurers per patient

rootGroups.name: Declaration, Financing and Insight Data
rootGroups.description: The money side of care and the insight it produces: declaration claims generated from the agenda and submitted through Vecozo under GDS801 or the zorgprestatiemodel, the eligibility checks and return messages around them, patient invoices and Mollie payments, the insurer contracts and municipal Jeugdwet and WMO assignments that decide tariffs and limits, the practice KPI snapshots behind the BI dashboards and the pseudonymised extracts delivered to quality registers. These assets carry the 7-year fiscal retention duty and NZa registration obligations on top of the AVG.

subGroups.name: Claims and Return Messages
subGroups.description: The declaration lifecycle from eligibility check to accepted claim: COV results, GDS801 and zorgprestatiemodel claims, and the Vecozo return messages that decide whether the practice is paid.

assets.name: Declaration Claim
assets.description: One claim for delivered care to a financier: for paramedics a GDS801 declaration with treatment lines derived from completed appointments (performance code, date, practitioner AGB, diagnosis code, referral or DTF indication, treatment count, tariff and contract reference); for GGZ a zorgprestatiemodel claim with consults, group sessions, setting, professional category, zorgvraagtypering and, from 2026, the mandatory referral date; for youth care and WMO a municipal declaration under the iJw or iWmo standard. Each claim carries its batch, submission state, Vecozo acknowledgement, return-message outcome, corrections and credit lines, and the payment expectation. Generated by the Declaration Engine (decl), registered for GGZ by Zorgprestatiemodel Registration and Compliance (zpmc) and Youth Care and Municipal Contracting (jzrg), transported by the Vecozo Gateway (vcgw) and reconciled by Billing Services (bils).
assets.businessMeaning: The revenue event of the practice and the platform's most audited artefact: HCI processed €500 million+ in annual declarations by 2022, and first-time acceptance is the KPI practices judge their software by.
assets.accessScope: practice owners, application managers and administrative staff of the tenant; billing-service operators of HCI for customers who outsource; the Vecozo gateway for transport; practitioners see their own claim lines; BSN visible only on the claim itself

interfaces.name: declaration-claim api
interfaces.description: Claim generation from registered appointments and consults, validation against contract and standard rules, batch assembly, submission state, correction and credit-line, and return-message reconciliation API used by the declaration engine, the Vecozo gateway, billing services, GGZ registration, municipal contracting and dashboards.

interfaces.name: declaration events
interfaces.description: Claim generated, validation failed, batch submitted, acknowledged by Vecozo, accepted, rejected, corrected and paid events consumed by billing services, patient invoicing for uncovered remainders, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: GDS801 and zorgprestatiemodel declaration files
interfaces.description: GDS801 declaration files and zorgprestatiemodel claim batches submitted to insurers through Vecozo, iJw and iWmo declaration messages to municipalities, and declaration overviews for the practice's accountant.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year under the fiscal retention duty and NZa registration rules; corrected versions kept alongside the original; claim lines that evidence treatment kept with the dossier for the WGBO term
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the addressed insurer or municipality through Vecozo or the Gemeentelijk Gegevensknooppunt only; summaries shared with the practice's accountant and Twinfield; never shared with partners or between tenants

assets.name: Insurance Eligibility Check
assets.description: The result of a Controle op Verzekeringsrecht (COV) request to Vecozo for a patient on a given date: insurer and UZOVI code, policy and package type, supplementary insurance covering physiotherapy or dietetics sessions, the BSN verification outcome, the response timestamp and validity, and the derived expectation of how many treatments are covered before the patient pays. Mastered in Vecozo Gateway and Insurance Eligibility (vcgw), executed automatically at intake and before each declaration batch, and written back into the patient profile as the current insurer.
assets.businessMeaning: A COV check before treatment is the cheapest way to prevent a rejected claim and an unexpected patient invoice; its freshness is a precondition of first-time acceptance.
assets.accessScope: front-desk and administrative staff of the tenant; the declaration engine; the patient sees their own insurer status in the app; raw Vecozo responses readable only by the gateway

interfaces.name: eligibility api
interfaces.description: COV request per patient and date, cached result lookup, coverage expectation and insurer-change detection API used by the agenda at intake, the dossier, the declaration engine and patient invoicing.

interfaces.name: eligibility events
interfaces.description: Check completed, insurer changed, no coverage found and BSN mismatch events consumed by the patient profile, the declaration engine, invoicing and front-desk notifications.

interfaces.name: COV messages
interfaces.description: COV request and response messages exchanged with Vecozo and kept in the message mirror as proof of the check performed before declaration.

governance.retention: kept 7 years with the claims that relied on the check; raw response messages kept in the mirror for the same term
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with Vecozo only; result shown to the tenant and the patient; never shared with partners

assets.name: Return Message
assets.description: A retourbericht from an insurer or municipality through Vecozo or the Gemeentelijk Gegevensknooppunt about a submitted batch: per claim line the acceptance or rejection code and reason (Vektis return codes such as unknown insured, contract missing, treatment limit exceeded, referral date missing under the 2026 zorgprestatiemodel rules), the approved amount, the expected payment date, and the working state that billing-service operators or practice staff give it (analysed, corrected and resubmitted, written off, disputed with the insurer). Mastered in Vecozo Gateway and Insurance Eligibility (vcgw), which retrieves, parses and stores every retourbericht under the tenant's certificate; linked line by line to the declaration claim by the Declaration Engine (decl) and worked, for practices that outsource billing, in Billing Services and Return-message Handling (bils), which adds the working state and recovery statistics.
assets.businessMeaning: Return messages are where rejected revenue is recovered or lost: the rejection rate and time-to-resubmission are the operational KPIs of both practices and HCI's billing service.
assets.accessScope: administrative staff and owners of the tenant; HCI billing-service operators for customers who outsource; the declaration engine for reconciliation; practitioners see rejection reasons on their own lines

interfaces.name: return-message api
interfaces.description: Return message ingestion and parsing, line-level linking to claims, rejection-reason taxonomy, work-queue state and resubmission API used by billing services, the declaration engine, the support desk and dashboards.

interfaces.name: return message events
interfaces.description: Return message received, line accepted, line rejected, resubmission due, dispute opened and written off events consumed by the declaration engine, invoicing for patient remainders, billing-service work queues and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: Vecozo return messages
interfaces.description: Retourberichten as received from Vecozo and iJw/iWmo return messages from municipalities, stored unchanged in the message mirror, plus rejection overviews sent to practices.

governance.retention: kept 7 years with the claims they answer under the fiscal retention duty; work-queue notes kept for the same term
governance.sharingPolicy: received from insurers and municipalities only; shown to the tenant and to HCI billing-service operators under the service agreement; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Invoices, Payments and Contracts
subGroups.description: Patient invoices and Mollie payments for uninsured and remainder care, and the contracts with insurers and municipalities that fix tariffs, limits and administrative conditions.

assets.name: Patient Invoice
assets.description: An invoice from the practice to a patient or a paying third party for care not covered by insurance, remainders after a rejected or capped claim, no-show fees where the practice applies them, group-programme and subscription charges and products such as insoles or supports: sequential invoice number per practice, lines with performance codes and VAT treatment, payment terms, delivery channel (e-mail, patient app, print), payment status, reminders and hand-over to collection. Mastered in Patient Invoicing and Payments (pinv), fed by Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions (grpm), settled by Mollie transactions and exported to Twinfield for the accountant.
assets.businessMeaning: Direct patient revenue and the practice's own sales ledger: invoice lines name the treatment and are therefore health data, correct numbering and VAT treatment are a fiscal duty, and app-based payment is what makes the small amounts collectable.
assets.accessScope: administrative staff and owners of the tenant; the patient for their own invoices in the app; HCI billing-service operators under the service agreement; the accountant through the Twinfield export

interfaces.name: patient-invoice api
interfaces.description: Invoice creation from appointments, remainders and programme charges, numbering, PDF rendering, delivery, payment-link generation, reminder and credit-note API used by invoicing, the patient app, group programmes and the accounting export.

interfaces.name: invoice events
interfaces.description: Invoice issued, delivered, viewed, paid, overdue, reminded, credited and handed to collection events consumed by payments, the patient app, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: invoice documents and accounting export
interfaces.description: Invoice PDFs for patients, UBL or PDF copies for third-party payers and the periodic sales-ledger export to Twinfield and other accounting packages.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year under the Dutch fiscal retention duty; invoice PDFs archived in the document store for the same term
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the patient or paying party, the practice's accountant through the export and Mollie for payment collection; never shared with insurers or partners

assets.name: Payment Transaction
assets.description: One payment or refund against a patient invoice or subscription: Mollie payment identifier and method (iDEAL, credit card, SEPA direct debit for subscriptions), amount, status transitions (open, paid, failed, expired, refunded, charged back), settlement reference and payout batch, the invoice lines it settles, pin-terminal payments registered at the desk and manual bank transfers matched by hand. Mastered in Patient Invoicing and Payments (pinv), ingested through Mollie webhooks and reconciled against the invoice and the Twinfield export.
assets.businessMeaning: Every automatically matched payment is an invoice nobody had to chase; payment status is what turns a patient invoice into cash and what the accountant reconciles.
assets.accessScope: administrative staff and owners of the tenant; the patient for their own payments in the app; the Mollie integration and the accounting export; card and bank details never stored, only Mollie references

interfaces.name: payment api
interfaces.description: Payment-link creation, status lookup, webhook ingestion from Mollie, refund, desk-payment registration and invoice settlement API used by invoicing, the patient app, group programmes and the accounting export.

interfaces.name: payment events
interfaces.description: Payment initiated, paid, failed, refunded, charged back and payout settled events consumed by invoicing, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: payment settlements
interfaces.description: Mollie settlement reports and the payment lines inside the Twinfield export used for bank reconciliation by the practice's accountant.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year with the invoices they settle; Mollie references kept for the same term
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with Mollie under its processing terms; shown to the tenant and the patient; exported to the practice's accountant; never shared with insurers or other partners

assets.name: Insurer Contract
assets.description: The agreement between a practice or institution and a health insurer for a contract year, or the uncontracted tariff position when there is none: insurer and UZOVI code, contracted performance codes and tariffs per discipline, treatment limits and chronic-list rules, administrative conditions (measurement instruments, patient surveys, Keurmerk or PLUS status), for GGZ the zorgprestatiemodel tariff percentages per setting and professional category, budget ceilings and turnover caps, and the contract documents themselves. Mastered by GGZ Registration and Financing in Zorgprestatiemodel Registration and Compliance (zpmc) for CRS and used by the Declaration Engine (decl) to validate every claim line against the tariff and conditions in force.
assets.businessMeaning: The contract is the rule book every claim is validated against: an outdated tariff table or missed condition turns into rejected batches and lost quality bonuses at year end.
assets.accessScope: practice owners and application managers of the tenant; HCI billing-service and implementation staff who load contract tables; the declaration engine for validation; contract tables per insurer maintained centrally by HCI

interfaces.name: insurer-contract api
interfaces.description: Contract and tariff lookup per insurer, performance code, discipline and date, limit and condition rules, budget-ceiling monitoring and contract-year rollover API used by the declaration engine, GGZ registration, dashboards and tenant configuration.

interfaces.name: contract events
interfaces.description: Contract loaded, tariff table updated, ceiling threshold reached, condition unmet and contract year closed events consumed by the declaration engine, dashboards and support tooling.

interfaces.name: contract and tariff documents
interfaces.description: Contract PDFs and insurer tariff sheets uploaded per practice, and the yearly NZa tariff and Vektis code tables distributed by HCI to all tenants.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the contract year with the claims validated against it; tariff table versions kept indefinitely for historical claim reconstruction
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant and HCI; NZa and Vektis reference tables are public; contract terms never shared between tenants or with partners

assets.name: Municipal Assignment
assets.description: A toewijzing from a municipality for youth care under the Jeugdwet or support under the Wmo 2015 for one client: municipality and gemeentecode, product code and volume or budget, start and end dates, the referrer (GP, gemeentelijke toegang, gecertificeerde instelling or court), the iJw or iWmo message chain (JW301/JW302 assignment request and confirmation, JW305/JW307 start and stop of care, JW303 declaration) with message status, contract and tariff reference per municipality or region and the woonplaatsbeginsel determination. Mastered in Youth Care and Municipal Contracting (jzrg) in CRS and the precondition for every municipal declaration claim.
assets.businessMeaning: Without a valid assignment there is no financing for youth care: institutions with dozens of municipal contracts depend on this record to know what may be delivered and declared.
assets.accessScope: zorgadministratie staff and application managers of the institution; the treating professionals for their own clients; the declaration engine; BSN visible only inside the iJw/iWmo messages

interfaces.name: municipal-assignment api
interfaces.description: Assignment request and confirmation, start and stop of care, volume and budget monitoring, municipality contract lookup and woonplaatsbeginsel check API used by municipal contracting, the CRS dossier, the declaration engine and institution reporting.

interfaces.name: assignment events
interfaces.description: Assignment requested, confirmed, care started, volume threshold reached, care stopped and assignment expired events consumed by the declaration engine, treatment plans, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: iJw and iWmo messages
interfaces.description: iJw and iWmo standard messages exchanged with municipalities through the Gemeentelijk Gegevensknooppunt and VECOZO, kept unchanged in the message mirror.

governance.retention: kept 20 years as part of the youth-care dossier under the Jeugdwet and WGBO retention rules and 7 years with the municipal claims it supports
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with the responsible municipality only through the iJw/iWmo standards; visible to the institution; never shared with insurers or partners

subGroups.name: Insight and Quality Registers
subGroups.description: The KPI snapshots behind practice and institution dashboards and the pseudonymised extracts delivered to LDF, Keurmerk and benchmark registers.

assets.name: Practice KPI Snapshot
assets.description: A materialised set of management figures per tenant and period: production and revenue per practitioner, location and insurer, treatment duration and treatments per episode against guideline norms, referrer volumes, waiting-list length and time to first appointment, online-booking and portal-activation shares, declaration acceptance and rejection rates, outstanding patient invoices, contract utilisation against ceilings, and for GGZ institutions productivity per team, waiting times against the 14-week Treeknorm and financier mix. Computed by Practice BI Dashboards and Reporting (bidb) from treatment episodes, appointments, claims and invoices, refreshed nightly and comparable across periods.
assets.businessMeaning: Dashboards turn registrations into decisions about staffing, contracts and referrer relations; the snapshot is also the layer where practice owners judge whether HCI One is worth switching to.
assets.accessScope: practice owners, application managers and team leads of the tenant; practitioners for their own figures; HCI product teams for pseudonymised platform aggregates only

interfaces.name: practice-kpi api
interfaces.description: Dashboard query per tenant, period, practitioner, location, insurer and referrer, drill-down to episode level within the tenant, export and scheduled report API used by the BI dashboards, the Zorgverlener App and institution reporting.

interfaces.name: kpi refresh events
interfaces.description: Snapshot refreshed, threshold alert (ceiling, waiting time, rejection rate) raised and scheduled report sent events consumed by notifications and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: management reports
interfaces.description: Scheduled PDF and spreadsheet reports for practice owners, institution boards and contract managers, and benchmark comparisons returned from ParaBench-style registers where the practice participates.

governance.retention: snapshots kept 5 years for trend comparison; rebuilt at any time from the underlying assets; no patient identifiers stored at snapshot level
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant; aggregate benchmarks shared across tenants only after anonymisation and with the practice's participation; never shared with insurers per practice without the owner's export

assets.name: Quality Data Extract
assets.description: A pseudonymised delivery to a quality register: the monthly LDF (Landelijke Database Fysiotherapie) extract with episodes, diagnoses, treatments and measurement results per opted-in patient, Keurmerk Fysiotherapie practice-register deliveries, patient-survey triggers to Qualiview and MediQuest, and benchmark submissions for other disciplines, each with the pseudonymisation key version, the consent evaluation per record, record counts, delivery timestamp, register acknowledgement and validation errors returned. Produced by Quality Data Delivery (qdat) from measurement results and episodes after checking data-sharing consent, and required for Keurmerk membership and many insurer contracts.
assets.businessMeaning: The extract is how practices keep their Keurmerk and insurer quality status: a missed or rejected monthly delivery costs contract conditions, and a delivery without consent is a breach.
assets.accessScope: the quality data module and the practice owner for delivery status; HCI insight-and-quality staff for validation errors; pseudonymised content readable only by the register; pseudonym keys held in the vault

interfaces.name: quality-data api
interfaces.description: Extract generation per register and month, consent evaluation report, pseudonymisation, delivery status and validation-error API used by quality data delivery, dashboards and the support desk.

interfaces.name: quality data events
interfaces.description: Extract generated, delivered, acknowledged, rejected with errors and consent excluded records counted events consumed by dashboards, the support desk and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: LDF monthly extract and register deliveries
interfaces.description: The monthly LDF extract file, Keurmerk register deliveries, Qualiview and MediQuest survey triggers and the benchmark and validation files returned by the registers, exchanged over secure file transfer.

governance.retention: extract files deleted 90 days after acknowledged delivery; delivery metadata and consent evaluation kept 7 years as evidence of lawful disclosure; pseudonym keys rotated per register rules
governance.sharingPolicy: delivered to the named register only under the register's data agreement and the patient's opt-in consent; never re-identified by HCI; never shared with insurers or partners

rootGroups.name: Mental Health Care and E-health Data
rootGroups.description: The GGZ-specific dossier content of HCI CRS and the e-health layer that Embloom, Emogy, NICE Connect and the exercise partners add to every discipline: multidisciplinary treatment plans and medication records, the questionnaire and intervention library of 500+ questionnaires and 450 interventions, assigned blended-care programmes and the home-task progress patients generate, video sessions and remote-care trajectories, and the links to exercise programmes in Physitrack and similar apps. Psychological questionnaire answers and medication are among the most sensitive data on the platform.

subGroups.name: GGZ Treatment
subGroups.description: The treatment plan that coordinates professionals and settings under the zorgprestatiemodel, and the medication record kept by psychiatrists and nurses in CRS.

assets.name: Treatment Plan
assets.description: The agreed plan for a GGZ or youth-care client in HCI CRS: main diagnosis group and zorgvraagtypering (HoNOS+ based), treatment goals in the client's words, the interventions and e-health modules chosen, the multidisciplinary team with the regiebehandelaar and co-treating professionals per zorgprestatiemodel category, planned settings (outpatient, group, day treatment, clinical, outreach) and frequency, crisis and safety agreements, evaluation moments with ROM, the client's and representative's agreement and signature, and the versions produced at each evaluation. Mastered in Treatment Plans and Multidisciplinary Coordination (trpl), it frames the treatment episode, feeds Zorgprestatiemodel Registration and Compliance (zpmc) with the setting and professional attributes every consult must carry, and triggers programme assignment in Embloom.
assets.businessMeaning: The plan is where care and financing meet in GGZ: settings, professionals and evaluation moments recorded here are what the NZa and insurers expect every declared consult to be consistent with.
assets.accessScope: the regiebehandelaar and multidisciplinary team members of the institution or practice; the client and representative for their own plan in the client portal; zorgadministratie for setting and professional attributes only; never visible to other tenants

interfaces.name: treatment-plan api
interfaces.description: Plan create and version, goal and intervention management, team and regiebehandelaar assignment, setting and frequency, evaluation scheduling with ROM, client agreement and signature API used by the CRS dossier, zorgprestatiemodel registration, the client portal, Embloom programme assignment and institution reporting.

interfaces.name: treatment plan events
interfaces.description: Plan drafted, agreed by client, regiebehandelaar changed, evaluation due, evaluation completed, plan revised and treatment ended events consumed by the declaration engine, ROM orchestration, e-health programmes, the client portal and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: treatment plan documents
interfaces.description: Signed plan PDFs for the client and representative, plan summaries inside referral-back letters through ZorgDomein or ZorgMail and plan data exposed to the client's PGO under MedMij authorisation.

governance.retention: kept 20 years after the last change to the file under the WGBO and Jeugdwet retention rules; every version kept because declared consults must remain explainable against the plan in force
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating institution or practice; setting and professional attributes shared with insurers and municipalities inside claims; summaries shared with referrers on release; exposed to the client's PGO only under MedMij authorisation

assets.name: Medication Record
assets.description: The medication overview kept for a GGZ client in CRS and mirrored for a patient in Uw Zorg Online: current and historical prescriptions with drug, dose, frequency and prescriber, start and stop reasons, allergies and intolerances, interactions and contra-indications checked against the G-Standaard, lab monitoring for clozapine and lithium where relevant, the medication verification done at admission and discharge, and the actual dispensing overview retrieved from the pharmacy through the AIS connector or the LSP. Mastered in Medication Management (medm) for CRS and consumed by Repeat Prescriptions and Medication Overview (rxrp) so a patient sees one overview in the app.
assets.businessMeaning: Medication safety in GGZ depends on one current overview across prescriber, pharmacy and client; it is also the record a psychiatrist is personally accountable for.
assets.accessScope: prescribing psychiatrists, physicians and nurse specialists of the tenant; treating professionals of the client's team for reading; the patient for their own overview in the app; pharmacies only through the AIS connector for their own dispensing data

interfaces.name: medication-record api
interfaces.description: Prescription create, modify and stop, interaction and allergy check, medication verification, dispensing overview retrieval and patient-facing overview API used by medication management, the CRS dossier, repeat prescriptions in the patient app and the pharmacy connectors.

interfaces.name: medication events
interfaces.description: Prescription issued, changed, stopped, interaction alert raised, verification completed and dispensing received events consumed by the dossier, the patient app, the audit log and the warehouse (counts only).

interfaces.name: prescription and dispensing messages
interfaces.description: Electronic prescriptions to pharmacies and dispensing overviews received through the AIS connectors and the Landelijk Schakelpunt, and medication summaries inside discharge letters and the client's PGO (MedMij medication resources).

governance.retention: kept 20 years after the last change to the file under the WGBO; prescription messages kept in the mirror for the same term
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the dispensing pharmacy through the connector and with the GP on release; shown to the patient in Uw Zorg Online and exposed to the PGO under MedMij authorisation; never shared with insurers beyond the claim attributes

subGroups.name: E-health Content and Programmes
subGroups.description: The Embloom library of questionnaires and interventions, the blended-care programmes assigned from it, and the progress patients and clients generate at home in Embloom, Emogy and the patient apps.

assets.name: Questionnaire Definition
assets.description: One instrument in the Embloom library of 500+ questionnaires or a measurement instrument configured in the paramedical EPDs: items, response scales, skip logic, scoring algorithm and subscales, norm tables per population, licence holder and licence terms (free, paid per administration, association-licensed), language versions, validity references, the disciplines and pathway steps it is recommended for, and its version history. Mastered in the Questionnaire and Intervention Library (qlib) and consumed by Measurement Instruments and PROMs (meas) and ROM and Questionnaire Orchestration for GGZ (romq) so that a score in the dossier always refers to a known instrument version.
assets.businessMeaning: The library is Embloom's core asset and the reason questionnaires are fully integrated in the EPD: every measurement result is only as valid as the definition and norms it was scored with.
assets.accessScope: the Embloom content team for authoring and licensing; tenant application managers to enable instruments; every practitioner for use; licence terms enforced per organisation

interfaces.name: questionnaire-definition api
interfaces.description: Instrument catalogue and search, item and scoring definition, norm lookup, licence check per organisation and version comparison API used by measurement instruments, ROM orchestration, blended-care programmes and the patient apps.

interfaces.name: questionnaire library events
interfaces.description: Instrument published, version updated, norm table replaced, licence changed and instrument retired events consumed by measurement instruments, ROM orchestration and tenant configuration.

interfaces.name: instrument packages
interfaces.description: Instrument definition packages imported from licence holders and exported to partner EPDs that use Embloom outside HCI, and licence usage reports to rights holders.

governance.retention: all versions kept indefinitely so historical results remain interpretable; licence usage records kept 7 years for settlement with rights holders
governance.sharingPolicy: shared library available to every HCI tenant and to Embloom's ~2,500 partner organisations under licence; instrument content used under the terms of the rights holders; no personal data

assets.name: E-health Programme
assets.description: A blended-care programme assigned to a patient or client: the intervention modules from the 450 Embloom interventions or a discipline programme, the sequence and schedule of sessions, exercises, psycho-education and questionnaires, the therapist's tailoring and feedback moments, the delivery channel (Embloom portal, Emogy app, Uw Zorg Online, e-mail link), the client's activation status and the programme's own outcome evaluation. Also the library-side blueprint from which assignments are created. Mastered in Blended Care Programme Builder and Monitoring (bldc), built from content in the Questionnaire and Intervention Library (qlib) and delivered on the Emogy Behavioural Support App (emgy) and other channels; linked to the treatment plan or episode it belongs to.
assets.businessMeaning: Blended care is how GGZ and paramedical practices treat more people with the same staff: the assigned programme is the contract between therapist and client about what happens between sessions.
assets.accessScope: the treating professional and team for their own clients; the client for their own programme in the app or portal; the content team for anonymised usage statistics; blueprints readable by every tenant that licenses them

interfaces.name: e-health-programme api
interfaces.description: Blueprint catalogue, programme assignment and tailoring, schedule and channel selection, therapist feedback, activation status and outcome evaluation API used by the programme builder, the CRS dossier, the paramedical EPDs, Emogy, the patient apps and institution reporting.

interfaces.name: programme events
interfaces.description: Programme assigned, activated by client, module unlocked, feedback given, programme completed and programme abandoned events consumed by home-task progress, the dossier, the client portal, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: programme exports
interfaces.description: Programme summaries inside treatment reports and dossier exports, and anonymised programme usage reports for content licensing and research partners.

governance.retention: assignments kept 20 years with the dossier under the WGBO; blueprints kept in all versions; anonymised usage statistics kept indefinitely
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating tenant and the client; blueprints shared across tenants under licence; anonymised usage shared with content partners and research institutions; never shared with insurers

assets.name: Home Task Progress
assets.description: What a patient or client actually did at home: completion of programme sessions and exercises, answers to psycho-education checks and reflections, diary entries and mood ratings inside a module, exercise sets and repetitions reported from Physitrack or another exercise app, Emogy behavioural support interactions, NICE Connect remote-care tasks, reminders sent and ignored, and the therapist's review status of each item. Mastered in Exercise Programme Integration (exrc) as the one normalised progress feed from every exercise and e-health source, written by the Emogy Behavioural Support App (emgy) and the partner adapters, aggregated per programme by Blended Care Programme Builder and Monitoring (bldc) and surfaced to the therapist as adherence signals and to the patient as progress.
assets.businessMeaning: Adherence is the difference between a programme that helps and a link nobody opened; progress data is what lets a therapist intervene early and what shows payers that remote care works.
assets.accessScope: the treating professional and team; the patient or client for their own progress; the content team and remote-care team for anonymised adherence statistics; exercise partners see only the tasks they deliver

interfaces.name: home-task-progress api
interfaces.description: Task completion and answer submission, exercise result ingestion from partner apps, adherence summary per programme and client, reminder scheduling and therapist review API used by the programme builder, Emogy, exercise integration, the patient apps and the dossier.

interfaces.name: progress events
interfaces.description: Task completed, exercise reported, mood rating submitted, reminder ignored, adherence dropped below threshold and therapist reviewed events consumed by the dossier, notifications, the client portal and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: partner exercise results
interfaces.description: Exercise adherence and result files received from Physitrack, Physiotrack and Fysio AI through the partner API and merged into the progress record.

governance.retention: kept 20 years with the dossier where the therapist has reviewed it as part of treatment; raw reminder and interaction logs deleted after 2 years; anonymised adherence statistics kept indefinitely
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the treating tenant and the client; exercise-task results exchanged with the delivering partner app under a processing agreement; anonymised adherence shared with content partners; never shared with insurers per client

subGroups.name: Remote Care
subGroups.description: Video consultations and NICE Connect remote-care trajectories, and the links between EPD episodes and exercise programmes in partner apps.

assets.name: Video Session
assets.description: One planned or held video consultation between a professional and a patient, client or family group: linked appointment and episode, participants and their join links, the video provider session identifier, start, end and connection quality, waiting-room and identity confirmation, screen-sharing and questionnaire use during the call, the professional's note reference and the consent to record where a recording is ever made for supervision. Mastered in Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories (vidc), created from the agenda and the CRS client portal and available in Quli for secure messaging and video with the care network. Media streams are end-to-end encrypted and by default not stored.
assets.businessMeaning: Video consultation keeps treatment going when the patient cannot travel and is a reimbursable consult under both GDS801 and the zorgprestatiemodel when properly registered.
assets.accessScope: the professional and participants of the session; front-desk staff for scheduling; the remote-care team for connection-quality metadata only; recordings, where made, readable only by the professional under the recorded consent

interfaces.name: video-session api
interfaces.description: Session creation from an appointment, participant links, waiting-room and identity confirmation, in-call questionnaire launch, quality telemetry and consult registration API used by video consultation, the agenda, the CRS client portal, Quli and the declaration engine.

interfaces.name: video session events
interfaces.description: Session scheduled, participant joined, session ended, connection failed and consult registered for declaration events consumed by the agenda, the dossier, the declaration engine and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: session recordings
interfaces.description: Exceptional recordings made for supervision or training with explicit consent, stored encrypted in the document store and deleted on the agreed date.

governance.retention: session metadata kept 20 years with the dossier as evidence of the consult; media streams not stored; connection telemetry deleted after 90 days; consented recordings deleted on the agreed date and at most after 1 year
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the tenant and the participants; consult registration shared with insurers inside claims; video provider processes streams under a processing agreement inside the EU; never shared with partners

assets.name: Remote Care Trajectory
assets.description: A remote follow-up trajectory in NICE Connect for a patient after discharge or alongside hospital treatment, such as the Amsterdam UMC premature infant network or a German rehabilitation centre programme: the coordinating hospital or centre and the involved first-line therapists, the protocol with scheduled measurements, questionnaires, video contacts and home tasks, thresholds and alert rules, the multidisciplinary review moments, the parents' or patient's app enrolment and the trajectory status and outcome. Mastered in Video Consultation and NICE Connect Trajectories (vidc) and integrated with paraNICE next to the hospital information system so the coordinator sees the whole network.
assets.businessMeaning: Remote trajectories are what let a hospital department follow hundreds of patients at home with one coordinator, and the model HCI wants insurers to reimburse as prevention and monitoring programmes.
assets.accessScope: the coordinating department and the therapists enrolled in the network; the patient or parents for their own trajectory in the app; hospital information systems only through the paraNICE connector for their own patients

interfaces.name: remote-care-trajectory api
interfaces.description: Trajectory enrolment and protocol assignment, network membership across hospital and first-line therapists, threshold and alert configuration, review scheduling and outcome API used by NICE Connect, paraNICE, home-task progress, video consultation and department reporting.

interfaces.name: trajectory events
interfaces.description: Trajectory started, measurement out of range, review due, therapist added to network, trajectory completed and escalated to hospital events consumed by notifications, the dossier, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: trajectory reports
interfaces.description: Periodic trajectory reports to the hospital information system through the paraNICE connector and discharge or completion summaries to the GP through ZorgMail.

governance.retention: kept 20 years with the dossier under the WGBO; threshold and alert logs kept for the same term as clinical evidence
governance.sharingPolicy: shared between the coordinating hospital or centre and the enrolled therapists as one care network under a data-sharing agreement; summaries to the GP on release; German trajectories kept under the German centre's agreement inside the EU; never shared with insurers per patient

assets.name: Exercise Programme Link
assets.description: The connection between a treatment episode and an exercise programme prescribed in a partner app: the partner (Physitrack, Physiotrack, Fysio AI or another exercise partner), the partner programme identifier and version, the prescribing therapist, the patient's activation code or account link, the exercises, sets and frequency as prescribed, the synchronisation state of adherence and results back into home-task progress, and the partner licence used by the practice. Mastered in Exercise Programme Integration (exrc) and created from the dossier through the Partner API so that the therapist never re-enters patient details in the partner app.
assets.businessMeaning: Exercise programmes are the most used e-health in physiotherapy; the link is what makes 'integrate once, reach every label' concrete for partners and what spares therapists double entry.
assets.accessScope: the prescribing therapist and tenant; the patient for their own programme; the partner app for the linked programme only; the open-platform team for connection health without content

interfaces.name: exercise-programme-link api
interfaces.description: Programme prescription hand-off to the partner, patient activation, programme lookup and adherence synchronisation API used by exercise integration, the dossier, home-task progress and the patient apps.

interfaces.name: exercise link events
interfaces.description: Programme prescribed, patient activated in partner app, adherence synchronised, programme updated by therapist and link ended events consumed by home-task progress, the dossier and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: partner programme exchange
interfaces.description: Programme prescriptions and adherence result payloads exchanged with exercise partners through the partner API, and licence usage reports per practice.

governance.retention: kept with the dossier for the WGBO term as part of the prescribed treatment; partner activation codes deleted when the link ends
governance.sharingPolicy: patient name, contact and programme exchanged with the chosen exercise partner under a processing agreement and the practice's partner licence; never shared with other partners or insurers

rootGroups.name: Patient Environment Data
rootGroups.description: The consumer-scale side of the platform: the 4 million+ patient and client accounts in Uw Zorg Online and the CRS client portal, e-consults and secure messages, repeat prescription requests, digital triage sessions, and the Quli personal health environment with MedMij consents, imported health data, self-measurements and family sharing. Here the citizen is the data controller of their own PGO and HCI is a MedMij-certified DVZA, which reverses the usual access logic: the person decides who sees what.

subGroups.name: Uw Zorg Online
subGroups.description: The patient's account and the requests it generates towards GP practices, pharmacies, therapists and GGZ institutions: e-consults, repeat prescriptions, triage sessions.

assets.name: Client Portal Account
assets.description: The citizen-side account in Uw Zorg Online, the Quli app or the CRS client portal: the person's verified identity (DigiD or practice-issued activation with identity check at the desk), the linked care providers (GP practice, pharmacy, physiotherapist, GGZ institution) with each provider's activation state and permitted functions (e-consult, appointments, repeat prescriptions, record access, questionnaires), representative and child accounts, notification preferences and channels, terms acceptance, app version and device, and the account lifecycle from invitation to deactivation. Mastered in Patient App and Web Portal (pgoa) as the one account across Uw Zorg Online, Quli and the CRS client portal; GGZ Client Portal (cpor) activates it for an institution's clients and records the institution-specific portal status, and every other patient-environment brick references it.
assets.businessMeaning: Portal activation is the adoption metric for practices and institutions alike: each active account is a patient who books, asks and reads online instead of calling.
assets.accessScope: the citizen for their own account and linked children; each linked care provider for the activation state and functions of its own patients; HCI support inside a logged support session; identity assertions never readable

interfaces.name: client-portal-account api
interfaces.description: Invitation and activation, DigiD login hand-off, provider linking and function permissions, representative and child accounts, notification preferences and deactivation API used by the patient app, the CRS client portal, e-consult, appointments, repeat prescriptions, triage, network care and the HIS/AIS connectors.

interfaces.name: portal account events
interfaces.description: Account invited, activated, provider linked, function enabled, representative added, notification sent and account deactivated events consumed by the practice EPDs, dashboards, the audit log and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: activation exchange with practice systems
interfaces.description: Activation lists and patient-link confirmations exchanged with HIS and AIS systems (Pharmapartners, CGM, Sanday, HealthConnected) so a practice sees which patients are active online.

governance.retention: kept while the account is active and 2 years after deactivation to answer access requests; identity assertions deleted immediately after login; provider links removed when the practice ends the treatment relationship
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and each linked care provider for its own patients; never shared between providers except through the patient's own actions; never shared with partners or insurers

assets.name: E-consult Message
assets.description: A secure message thread between a patient or client and a care provider through Uw Zorg Online or the CRS client portal: the question with optional photos and attachments, the triage category and urgency flag, the practice mailbox or professional it was routed to, the answer and follow-up messages, read receipts, response-time measurement against the practice's promised term, the link to the HIS, AIS or EPD where the thread is filed, and the closure with an optional appointment or prescription outcome. Mastered in E-consult and Secure Messaging (econ), reused by the GGZ Client Portal (cpor) for client-practitioner messaging, and filed into the patient's record in the practice system through the connectors.
assets.businessMeaning: The e-consult replaces the phone call that GP practices, pharmacies and therapists want to avoid; response time is the patient's experience metric and the practice's workload metric.
assets.accessScope: the patient or client and their representative; the addressed practice or professional; HCI support only for delivery metadata, never message content; message bodies encrypted at rest

interfaces.name: e-consult api
interfaces.description: Thread create, message send with attachments, routing to mailbox or professional, answer and close, read receipt and response-time API used by the patient app, the CRS client portal, the practice EPDs and the HIS/AIS connectors.

interfaces.name: e-consult events
