interfaces.description: Consult submitted, routed, answered, escalated to appointment, closed and response term exceeded events consumed by notifications, the practice systems, dashboards and the warehouse (metadata only).

interfaces.name: e-consult filing
interfaces.description: E-consult threads filed into the GP, pharmacy or therapist system through the HIS/AIS and EPD connectors as correspondence in the patient record.

governance.retention: kept 20 years as part of the medical record of the practice that answered it under the WGBO; unanswered drafts deleted after 30 days; delivery metadata kept 2 years
governance.sharingPolicy: shared only between the patient and the addressed care provider; filed into that provider's system; never readable by other linked providers or HCI; never shared with partners

assets.name: Repeat Prescription Request
assets.description: A request from a patient in Uw Zorg Online to their GP practice or pharmacy for repeat medication: the medication lines selected from the medication overview retrieved from the pharmacy or GP system, quantity and preferred pickup or delivery, the addressed practice or pharmacy and its HIS/AIS, the request status (submitted, received by practice, approved, rejected with reason, ready for pickup, delivered) and the electronic prescription reference returned by the practice system. Mastered in Repeat Prescriptions and Medication Overview (rxrp), transported to Pharmapartners, CGM, Sanday, HealthConnected and other connected systems by the HIS/AIS connectors and consistent with the medication record.
assets.businessMeaning: Repeat prescriptions are the highest-volume routine contact for GP practices and pharmacies; digitising them is the front door's most tangible relief of phone traffic.
assets.accessScope: the patient and representative; the addressed GP practice or pharmacy; HCI support for status metadata only; medication lines readable only by the patient and the addressed provider

interfaces.name: repeat-prescription api
interfaces.description: Medication overview retrieval, request submission with selected lines, status tracking, rejection reason and pickup notification API used by the patient app, the HIS/AIS connectors and the medication overview.

interfaces.name: repeat prescription events
interfaces.description: Request submitted, received by practice, approved, rejected, ready for pickup and delivered events consumed by notifications, the medication overview, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: prescription request messages
interfaces.description: Repeat prescription request and status messages exchanged with GP and pharmacy information systems through the HIS/AIS connectors, kept in the message mirror.

governance.retention: kept 2 years after completion in the patient environment; the resulting prescription lives in the practice or pharmacy system under its own retention; message copies kept in the mirror for 2 years
governance.sharingPolicy: shared only with the addressed GP practice or pharmacy through its information system; never shared with other providers, partners or insurers

assets.name: Triage Session
assets.description: One run through digital triage in Uw Zorg Online or on a practice website, based on 'Moet ik naar de dokter?' style protocols and partner engines such as Quin: the complaint entry point, the questions asked and answers given, the urgency outcome and advice (self-care, e-consult, appointment, call now, emergency), the practice the session was started for, whether the patient converted the advice into an e-consult or appointment, and the session's anonymous or account-linked status. Mastered in Digital Triage (trig) and linked to the client-portal account when the patient is logged in; anonymous sessions started from a practice website run through the same triage service and keep no identity; nothing is stored in the website CMS.
assets.businessMeaning: Triage is HCI's stated investment area for absorbing routine demand: the session record shows whether the digital front door actually diverted a phone call or an unnecessary visit.
assets.accessScope: the patient for their own sessions; the addressed practice for sessions converted into a consult or appointment; the Uw Zorg Online team for anonymised protocol performance; triage engine partners process content under a processing agreement

interfaces.name: triage api
interfaces.description: Session start from app or website, protocol question flow, outcome and advice, conversion to e-consult or appointment and anonymised outcome statistics API used by digital triage, the patient app, practice websites and the e-consult module.

interfaces.name: triage events
interfaces.description: Session started, outcome reached, urgent advice given, converted to e-consult or appointment and abandoned events consumed by e-consult, appointment self-service, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: triage filing
interfaces.description: Triage summaries attached to the e-consult or appointment request filed into the practice system through the connectors.

governance.retention: account-linked sessions kept 2 years, or 20 years where the summary was filed into the medical record of the practice; anonymous sessions reduced to protocol statistics after 30 days
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the addressed practice only when the patient converts the advice; anonymised outcome statistics shared with triage protocol partners; never shared with insurers

subGroups.name: Personal Health Environment (Quli)
subGroups.description: The MedMij-certified PGO where the citizen holds the keys: consents and retrievals from care providers, imported FHIR data, self-measurements and diaries, and sharing with family and informal carers.

assets.name: MedMij Consent
assets.description: A citizen's authorisation under the MedMij afsprakenstelsel to retrieve or share health data between their Quli or Uw Zorg Online PGO and a care provider's system through a DVZA: the care provider and its DVZA endpoint from the MedMij zorgaanbiederslijst, the information standards and gegevensdiensten authorised (GP data, medication, lab results, GGZ data, self-measurements, paramedical data where available), the DigiD authentication and OAuth token references, grant and expiry dates, revocation, and the log of retrievals performed under the consent. Mastered in MedMij Data Exchange and Consent (pgom), maintained under HCI's own MedMij label as PGO and DVZA, and the precondition for every health-data import.
assets.businessMeaning: MedMij consent is the legal and technical key to the citizen's data across systems; keeping it correct is what the MedMij label and the Wegiz obligations of GP practices and GGZ institutions are audited on.
assets.accessScope: the citizen for their own consents; the Quli and MedMij team for endpoint and token metadata only; care providers see only that a retrieval was authorised and performed; tokens held encrypted and never displayed

interfaces.name: medmij-consent api
interfaces.description: Care provider lookup in the zorgaanbiederslijst, authorisation flow with DigiD, gegevensdienst selection, token lifecycle, revocation and retrieval-log API used by MedMij data exchange, health-data import, the PGO apps and the DVZA side for connected practices.

interfaces.name: medmij consent events
interfaces.description: Consent granted, retrieval performed, token refreshed, consent revoked and consent expired events consumed by health-data import, the audit log, dashboards and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: MedMij FHIR resources and logs
interfaces.description: FHIR resources retrieved and shared under the consent per MedMij information standard, and the MedMij-mandated logging of every exchange for the citizen's own overview and for label audits.

governance.retention: consent and retrieval logs kept as long as the PGO account exists and for the MedMij-required logging term after revocation; tokens deleted at revocation or expiry
governance.sharingPolicy: the citizen alone decides; exchanges happen only with the authorised care provider's DVZA under the MedMij afsprakenstelsel; HCI never uses the data for other purposes; never shared with insurers or partners

assets.name: Health Data Import
assets.description: Health data retrieved into the citizen's PGO from a care provider under a MedMij consent, or from HCI's own EPDs into Uw Zorg Online: FHIR resources per information standard (GP summary and journal, medication overview, lab results, allergies, GGZ treatment summary, hospital discharge letters, paramedical data where the provider discloses it, vaccination data), the source provider and retrieval moment, the raw resource as received and the normalised view shown in the app, deduplication across sources, and export to a file or another PGO when the citizen switches. Mastered in MedMij Data Exchange and Consent (pgom) and read by Self-measurements and Diaries (diar) to place measurements next to professional data; also the overview Uw Zorg Online shows for records and medication.
assets.businessMeaning: Imported data is the substance of the PGO promise 'see and share my health data on my own terms'; its correctness and completeness are what citizens judge a PGO by and what the Wegiz obliges providers to disclose.
assets.accessScope: the citizen for their own environment and the people they explicitly share with; HCI staff cannot read content, only retrieval metadata; encrypted per citizen

interfaces.name: health-data-import api
interfaces.description: Retrieval per gegevensdienst and provider, normalised timeline and medication overview, deduplication, per-record sharing state and portability export API used by MedMij data exchange, the PGO apps, self-measurements, network care and the Uw Zorg Online record view.

interfaces.name: health data import events
interfaces.description: Retrieval completed, new record available, retrieval failed at the provider, data exported and data deleted by citizen events consumed by notifications, the audit log and adoption dashboards (counts only).

interfaces.name: MedMij FHIR resources and portability exports
interfaces.description: FHIR bundles received from DVZAs per MedMij information standard, PDF and FHIR exports the citizen downloads or transfers to another PGO, and data disclosed by HCI's own EPDs as DVZA to other PGOs.

governance.retention: kept as long as the citizen keeps it in their PGO; deleted immediately on the citizen's instruction or account closure, with a 30-day recovery window; source providers keep their own records under their own retention
governance.sharingPolicy: controlled by the citizen: shown only to people and providers the citizen shares with; HCI as PGO provider never discloses or analyses content; never shared with insurers or partners

assets.name: Family Share Permission
assets.description: A grant by a Quli user to a family member, informal carer, mentor or professional to see or contribute to parts of their environment, the basis of Quli's network care: the invited person and their verified account, the scope (diaries, measurements, imported records, messages, agenda, e-health apps in the GGZ appwijzer) with read or write rights per part, time limits, the relationship type, representative status for children and clients under guardianship, acceptance, and revocation history. Mastered in Network Care and Family Sharing (netw) and evaluated on every read in the PGO, with the same model reused for IC aftercare networks and GGZ client networks.
assets.businessMeaning: Granular sharing is what makes Quli different from a records viewer: the client decides who in their network sees what, including the professional, which is the trust basis for youth and GGZ use.
assets.accessScope: the account holder for their own grants; the grantee for the parts granted; the Quli team for grant metadata only; representatives of minors and clients under guardianship according to the recorded status

interfaces.name: family-share api
interfaces.description: Invitation, scope and rights definition per environment part, acceptance, time-limited grants, representative status and revocation API used by network care, self-measurements, the PGO apps, secure messaging and video in Quli.

interfaces.name: sharing events
interfaces.description: Share invited, accepted, scope changed, access used by grantee and share revoked events consumed by the audit log, notifications and adoption dashboards (counts only).

governance.retention: kept while the environment exists; revoked grants kept in the history for 2 years so the account holder can see who had access; deleted with the environment
governance.sharingPolicy: controlled entirely by the account holder; never visible to care providers beyond their own granted scope; never shared with partners or insurers

assets.name: Self-measurement
assets.description: A value the citizen records or a connected device reports in Quli or Uw Zorg Online: blood pressure, weight, glucose, steps, mood and sleep diaries, pain scores, symptom diaries for GGZ, home exercise logs, with timestamp, source (manual, app, device through a partner integration), unit and reference range, the diary or programme it belongs to, comments and the sharing state per network member or care provider, and the MedMij self-measurement resource when shared with a provider. Mastered in Self-measurements and Diaries (diar), placed next to imported professional data from Health Data Import, and shared into the EPD or e-health programme where the professional has asked for it.
assets.businessMeaning: Self-measurements are the citizen's own contribution to their record and the raw material of remote monitoring; shared correctly they save a consult, shared wrongly they are a privacy incident.
assets.accessScope: the citizen and the network members they share with; the care provider only for measurements explicitly shared or requested inside a programme; the Quli team for anonymised usage statistics

interfaces.name: self-measurement api
interfaces.description: Measurement and diary entry, device and app import, timeline with reference ranges, sharing state per person and provider and MedMij self-measurement disclosure API used by self-measurements, network care, the PGO apps, blended-care programmes and remote-care trajectories.

interfaces.name: self-measurement events
interfaces.description: Measurement recorded, value out of range, diary streak, shared with provider and measurement deleted events consumed by remote-care alerts, notifications, home-task progress and the warehouse (counts only).

interfaces.name: measurement exchange
interfaces.description: MedMij self-measurement FHIR resources shared with a care provider and device data imported through partner integrations.

governance.retention: kept as long as the citizen keeps it; deleted on instruction or account closure; copies shared into a provider's EPD follow that dossier's WGBO retention
governance.sharingPolicy: controlled by the citizen; shared with providers only per measurement or programme; device partners process data under a processing agreement; never shared with insurers

rootGroups.name: Network, Platform and Operations Data
rootGroups.description: The data that connects HCI to the rest of Dutch healthcare and keeps the roll-up running: referral and secure messages with ZorgDomein, ZorgMail and hospital systems, the HIS and AIS connections to GP and pharmacy systems, partner API credentials and the integration events they generate, the Praktijkinfo practice websites, the configuration of every tenant and label on the multi-tenant runtime, the migration batches that move acquired labels into HCI One, and the support tickets of the onboarding and support desk. Little of it is medical, but most of it is security-critical: a leaked partner credential or a mis-mapped migration batch affects thousands of practices.

subGroups.name: Care Network and Partners
subGroups.description: Referrals and secure messages, GP and pharmacy system connections, partner API access and the integration events flowing through the open platform, plus the practice websites that serve as entry points.

assets.name: Referral Message
assets.description: A referral, reply or secure message exchanged with the care network: ZorgDomein referrals from a GP or specialist to a paramedical or GGZ provider with referral date, reason, referrer AGB and the patient's details, the acceptance or waiting-list reply, end-of-treatment and interim reports back to the referrer, ZorgMail secure e-mail (Edifact and secure mail) with attachments, hospital information system messages for paraNICE departments, and the message status from received through filed in the dossier to answered. Mastered in Referral and Secure Messaging Hub (zdom), matched to a patient and episode in the EPD or CRS, and the source of the referral date that every zorgprestatiemodel declaration must carry from 2026.
assets.businessMeaning: The referral is the start of most episodes and, since 2026, a mandatory attribute of every GGZ claim; closing the loop with a report is what keeps GPs referring to the practice.
assets.accessScope: the receiving practice or institution and its treating professionals; front-desk staff for intake; the referrer for their own referral and the reports sent back; the integration team for delivery metadata only

interfaces.name: referral-message api
interfaces.description: Inbound referral retrieval and matching to patient and episode, waiting-list reply, report composition and dispatch, secure message send and receive, and delivery status API used by the referral hub, the agenda for intake, the dossier, treatment plans, the declaration engine for the referral date and paraNICE.

interfaces.name: referral events
interfaces.description: Referral received, matched to patient, accepted, placed on waiting list, report sent, message delivery failed and referral loop closed events consumed by the agenda, the dossier, dashboards on referrers and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: ZorgDomein referral messages and ZorgMail traffic
interfaces.description: ZorgDomein referral and reply messages, ZorgMail Edifact and secure mail with attachments, and HL7 messages exchanged with hospital information systems for paraNICE departments, all kept unchanged in the message mirror.

governance.retention: kept 20 years as part of the medical file it opened or reported on under the WGBO; transport metadata kept 2 years; undeliverable messages deleted after 90 days
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged only between the referrer and the addressed provider through ZorgDomein, ZorgMail or the hospital connector; referral date shared with insurers inside claims; never shared with partners

assets.name: HIS Connection
assets.description: The configured link between a GP practice, pharmacy or hospital department and the HCI platform: the practice and its information system (Pharmapartners Medicom and Pharmacom, CGM, Sanday, HealthConnected, Bricks, Vertimart, MicroHIS, ProMedico, or a hospital information system for paraNICE), connector type and protocol version, endpoint and certificate references in the vault, enabled functions (e-consult filing, appointment booking in the practice agenda, repeat prescriptions, record disclosure, patient activation, referral filing), synchronisation schedules, health status and error counts, and the practice's contract for Uw Zorg Online functions. Mastered in HIS/AIS and Hospital System Connectors (hisc) and used by every patient-environment brick to reach the right practice system for a patient.
assets.businessMeaning: The connectors are what make Uw Zorg Online the digital front door of thousands of GP practices and pharmacies; a broken connection means patients' requests silently stop reaching the practice.
assets.accessScope: the care-network integration team; the practice's application manager for their own connection and function settings; HIS/AIS vendors for their own connector versions; certificates and keys readable only by the connector services

interfaces.name: his-connection api
interfaces.description: Connection registration, function enablement, endpoint and certificate rotation, health and error status and patient-routing lookup API used by the connectors, the patient app, e-consult, appointments, repeat prescriptions, MedMij DVZA services and the support desk.

interfaces.name: connection events
interfaces.description: Connection activated, function enabled, synchronisation failed, error threshold exceeded, certificate expiring and connection ended events consumed by the support desk, security monitoring and dashboards.

interfaces.name: connector message exchange
interfaces.description: The message traffic with GP, pharmacy and hospital systems (patient lookups, appointment slots, prescriptions, record disclosures, HL7 messages) kept in the message mirror for troubleshooting and audit.

governance.retention: kept while the practice is connected and 2 years after; message mirror entries kept 2 years unless they are part of a medical file; keys destroyed at disconnection
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and the connected practice; connector specifications shared with HIS/AIS vendors under partner agreements; never shared with other practices

assets.name: Partner API Credential
assets.description: The registration of an integration partner on the HCI open platform: the partner organisation and its agreement, the applications registered (exercise apps such as Physitrack and Physiotrack, Fysio AI, questionnaire providers, quality registers such as Qualiview and MediQuest, Twinfield, Mollie, e-health providers such as Therapieland and Minddistrict for CRS, HIS/AIS vendors), OAuth client identifiers and secret references in the vault, granted scopes per label and function, the tenants that have enabled the partner and the consent basis, rate limits, webhook endpoints, sandbox versus production status, certification status against the API version and the key rotation history. Mastered in Partner API and Open Platform (papi) and referenced by Exercise Programme Integration (exrc) and the HIS/AIS connectors.
assets.businessMeaning: The credential is the contract between HCI and its ecosystem in executable form: scopes decide what a partner may touch across 40,000+ professionals' data, and its hygiene is a NEN 7510 audit item.
assets.accessScope: the open-platform team; the partner for its own application registrations and rotation; tenant application managers to enable or disable a partner for their tenant; secrets never displayed after creation

interfaces.name: partner registry api
interfaces.description: Partner and application registration, scope grant and review, tenant enablement, key rotation, sandbox promotion, webhook configuration and certification status API used by the partner API, the developer portal, tenant configuration and the support desk.

interfaces.name: partner credential events
interfaces.description: Partner registered, scope granted, tenant enabled partner, key rotated, rate limit exceeded, certification expired and partner offboarded events consumed by the audit log, security monitoring, integration event handling and the warehouse.

governance.retention: kept while the partner agreement is active and 7 years after offboarding as evidence of who had access; secrets destroyed at rotation or offboarding
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and the partner for its own registration; tenant enablement visible to the tenant; never shared between partners

assets.name: Integration Event
assets.description: One call or webhook across the open platform boundary: the partner application and tenant, the API version and operation (exercise programme prescribed, adherence pushed, questionnaire result delivered, invoice exported to Twinfield, payment webhook from Mollie, quality survey triggered, e-health module launched from CRS), request and response metadata, latency, outcome and error class, idempotency key, the domain event it produced or consumed, and the correlation to the audit log entry that names the patient or practitioner involved without duplicating their data. Mastered in Partner API and Open Platform (papi) and the basis of partner-facing availability and transaction metrics.
assets.businessMeaning: Integration events are how HCI proves the partner API is reliable through release changes and how a partner is billed or throttled; they are also the first place a broken connection shows up.
assets.accessScope: the open-platform team; partners for their own applications' events in the developer portal; tenant application managers for their own tenant's traffic; payloads containing personal data never stored, only references

interfaces.name: integration-event api
interfaces.description: Event query per partner, tenant, operation and period, error drill-down, replay of idempotent webhooks and partner availability and transaction statistics API used by the partner API, the developer portal, the support desk and dashboards.

interfaces.name: integration events
interfaces.description: Call succeeded, call failed, webhook delivered, webhook retry exhausted, rate limit hit and API version deprecated events consumed by security monitoring, the support desk, partner notifications and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: partner usage reports
interfaces.description: Monthly partner usage and availability reports for partner agreements and internal integration metrics.

governance.retention: raw events kept 13 months for troubleshooting and monthly statistics; aggregates kept 5 years; no payload content retained
governance.sharingPolicy: each partner sees only its own applications' events; tenants see their own traffic; aggregates internal to HCI; never shared with insurers

assets.name: Practice Website
assets.description: A Praktijkinfo practice website under Uw Zorg Online or an HCI label: the practice and its domain, theme and pages (team, locations, opening hours, treatments, tariffs, privacy statement), the embedded entry points (24/7 online booking against the agenda, e-consult and account activation, digital triage widget, repeat prescriptions for GP practices), forms and their routing, hosting, TLS and accessibility settings, analytics consent configuration, content versions and publication state. Mastered in Practice Websites (pweb), feeding Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders (obok) with booking requests and consuming free slots from the agenda without exposing patient names.
assets.businessMeaning: The website is where a new patient finds and books the practice; embedding booking, e-consult and triage in it is what makes it a front door rather than a brochure.
assets.accessScope: the practice's editors and owner; the open-platform team for hosting and templates; the public for published pages; form submissions routed to the practice and not retained on the site

interfaces.name: practice-website api
interfaces.description: Site and page management, theme and domain settings, entry-point configuration for booking, e-consult and triage, form routing and publication API used by practice websites, online booking, digital triage and tenant configuration.

interfaces.name: website events
interfaces.description: Site published, booking entry point used, form submitted, domain or certificate expiring and site archived events consumed by online booking, the support desk and adoption dashboards.

interfaces.name: site content and hosting
interfaces.description: Published static pages and assets served to the public, and domain and certificate records managed with the hosting provider.

governance.retention: content versions kept while the site exists and 1 year after cancellation; form submissions forwarded and not retained beyond 30 days; visitor analytics only under cookie consent and anonymised
governance.sharingPolicy: published pages are public; editor data internal to the practice and HCI; visitor analytics never shared with third parties

subGroups.name: Runtime, Migration and Support
subGroups.description: The configuration of every tenant and label on the multi-tenant cloud runtime, the migration batches that consolidate labels into HCI One, and the tickets of the onboarding, training and support desk.

assets.name: Tenant Configuration
assets.description: The definition of one practice, institution or label instance on the multi-tenant runtime: tenant identifier and label (HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE, CRS, Uw Zorg Online practice, Quli organisation, Embloom organisation), organisation details with KVK and AGB practice codes, locations, enabled modules and integrations (Vecozo, ZorgDomein, ZorgMail, MedMij, LDF, Twinfield, Mollie, partner apps), discipline and template settings, declaration parameters and contract references, feature flags and the HCI One rollout wave, data-residency zone, processing-agreement status and version, subscription and billing plan, and the runtime environment and database placement. Mastered in Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling (tnnt) and read by Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling (supp) on every ticket.
assets.businessMeaning: The tenant record is what isolates one practice's data from another's and what decides which of the many labels' behaviours a user gets; it is also the unit of HCI's subscription revenue and of the HCI One migration plan.
assets.accessScope: the cloud-runtime team and implementation consultants; the tenant's application manager for their own settings; the support desk for reading; billing for plan attributes; database placement and keys never visible to tenants

interfaces.name: tenant-configuration api
interfaces.description: Tenant provisioning, module and integration enablement, discipline and template settings, declaration parameters, feature flags and rollout wave, processing-agreement status and environment placement API used by every brick at request scoping, the support desk, migration tooling, the partner registry and billing.

interfaces.name: tenant events
interfaces.description: Tenant provisioned, module enabled, integration activated, feature flag changed, rollout wave assigned, processing agreement signed and tenant suspended or closed events consumed by all bricks, the support desk, the audit log and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: tenant exports
interfaces.description: Configuration exports for migration and audits, and subscription and usage lines for HCI's own invoicing.

governance.retention: kept while the tenant exists and 7 years after closure as evidence of the processing agreement and subscription; patient data of a closed tenant handed over or destroyed per the agreement
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and the tenant; configuration shared with implementation partners under agreement; never shared between tenants

assets.name: Migration Batch
assets.description: One controlled transfer of a practice's data from an acquired label or a competitor system into HCI One or CRS: source system and version (FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, Abakus, Podofile, Edevop, FysioLogic, Intramed or another export), the extraction and mapping profile, record counts per object (patients, practitioners, episodes, notes, measurements, appointments, open claims, invoices, documents), validation results and defect list, reconciliation counts between source and target, the practice's sign-off, the cut-over window and go-live date, rollback status, and the retention decision for the source data. Mastered in Multi-tenant Cloud Runtime and Label Migration Tooling (tnnt) and driven by the implementation consultants who take practices live without a forced migration deadline.
assets.businessMeaning: Migration batches are the operational core of the buy-and-build strategy: 'the best of every label without disrupting daily care' is decided by how many defects a batch carries at go-live.
assets.accessScope: the cloud-runtime team and the assigned implementation consultants; the practice owner for counts, defects and sign-off; source and staged data readable only by the migration services; never by support staff outside the project

interfaces.name: migration-batch api
interfaces.description: Batch planning, extraction and mapping profile selection, validation and defect management, reconciliation counts, dry-run and cut-over execution, sign-off and rollback API used by migration tooling, the support desk, onboarding projects and tenant configuration.

interfaces.name: migration events
interfaces.description: Batch extracted, validation completed, defect threshold exceeded, dry-run completed, cut-over started, go-live confirmed and rollback executed events consumed by the support desk, notifications, the audit log and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: migration exports and reports
interfaces.description: Source system exports and documents in the staging zone, mapping tables, validation and reconciliation reports for the practice's sign-off, and archived source data where the practice asked HCI to keep it.

governance.retention: batch metadata and reports kept 7 years as evidence of a lawful and complete transfer; staged source data deleted 90 days after sign-off unless the practice contracts archival; migrated medical data follows the WGBO term in the target
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and the migrating practice; source vendors involved only for export under the practice's instruction; never shared between practices

assets.name: Support Ticket
assets.description: A request handled by HCI's customer operations: support questions and incidents per label, onboarding and training tasks, migration issues, declaration return-message cases for billing-service customers, integration failures with Vecozo, ZorgDomein or a HIS, partner escalations, and security or privacy reports, with the tenant and reporting user, category and priority, the label and module, the support-session consent when a consultant needs to look into a tenant, linked audit entries, resolution steps, knowledge-article links, satisfaction score and resolution time against the service level. Mastered in Customer Support and Onboarding Tooling (supp), reading Tenant Configuration for context, and the source of the support-resolution and go-live metrics of the implementation and support team.
assets.businessMeaning: Support responsiveness is what keeps practices loyal through consolidation; ticket data shows where a label, a release or a migration wave creates friction before churn does.
assets.accessScope: the implementation and support team; the reporting user and tenant application manager for their own tickets; product teams for anonymised categories; ticket text must not contain patient data, and screenshots with patient data are stored only in the document store under the support-session consent

interfaces.name: support-ticket api
interfaces.description: Ticket creation from the apps, portals and e-mail, categorisation and routing, support-session consent and impersonation request, status and resolution, knowledge-article linking and satisfaction survey API used by the support desk, the Zorgverlener App, the partner developer portal and onboarding projects.

interfaces.name: ticket events
interfaces.description: Ticket opened, prioritised, escalated to a product team, support session started, resolved, reopened and service level breached events consumed by notifications, security monitoring for privacy reports and the warehouse.

interfaces.name: support attachments and reports
interfaces.description: Attachments and screenshots stored in the document store, monthly service reports per tenant or partner and incident reports for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 records.

governance.retention: kept 5 years after closure for service history and audit evidence; security and privacy incident tickets kept 7 years; attachments with patient data deleted 90 days after closure
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to HCI and the reporting tenant or partner; incident reports shared with certification auditors and, where required, with the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens; never shared between tenants

stores.name: Practice EPD DB
stores.description: Per-tenant relational schema (PostgreSQL-style, one schema per practice or label instance) for the paramedical practice management systems and HCI One: patients, practitioners, agenda and appointments, group programmes, treatment episodes, clinical notes, care-pathway instances and measurement results; BSN stored in encrypted columns readable only by the eligibility and declaration modules, row-level keys per practice so a therapist never reads another practice's dossier.

stores.name: CRS GGZ DB
stores.description: Relational schema per GGZ institution or independent practice on HCI CRS: client dossiers, treatment plans and multidisciplinary coordination, medication records, zorgprestatiemodel registrations, municipal assignments and iJw/iWmo message state, agenda and client-portal links; larger institutions run on a dedicated database instance, independent practitioners on a shared, row-keyed instance.

stores.name: Patient Platform DB
stores.description: Relational schema behind Uw Zorg Online and the CRS client portal: patient and client accounts, links to practices and care providers, e-consult threads, appointment requests, repeat prescription requests, triage sessions and notification state; keyed per citizen and per connected practice so a GP practice sees only its own patients' requests.

stores.name: Quli PGO DB
stores.description: Encrypted per-citizen schema for the Quli personal health environment: MedMij consents and retrieval logs, imported health data as FHIR resources, self-measurements and diary entries, network-care groups and family sharing permissions; the citizen holds the keys to their own environment, HCI staff cannot read content, only metadata needed for operations.

stores.name: E-health Content Store
stores.description: Document store for the Embloom library and Emogy content: 500+ questionnaire definitions with items, scoring rules and norm tables, 450 e-health interventions and treatment modules with versioned pages, exercises and media, programme blueprints and licence terms per organisation; contains no patient data.

stores.name: E-health Programme DB
stores.description: Relational schema for assigned blended-care programmes and remote care: programme assignments per patient or client, home-task progress and completion events, Emogy app state, NICE Connect trajectories, video-session metadata and exercise-programme links to Physitrack and other partners; linked to the practice EPD or CRS dossier by episode identifier.

stores.name: Declaration DB
stores.description: Relational schema for everything that leaves the practice as a claim: declaration claims with GDS801 or zorgprestatiemodel line items and lifecycle state, insurance eligibility (COV) results, insurer contracts and tariff tables, municipal assignments referenced by youth-care claims, and the return-message reconciliation state; locked per claim version once submitted.

stores.name: Vecozo Message Mirror
stores.description: Mirror of the message exchange with Vecozo and financiers as sent and received: GDS801 declaration files and zorgprestatiemodel claim batches, COV requests and answers, return messages (retourberichten) with rejection codes, iJw and iWmo messages exchanged with municipalities through the Gemeentelijk Gegevensknooppunt, kept as received for proof of submission.

stores.name: Invoicing and Payments DB
stores.description: Relational schema for patient invoices with sequential numbering per practice, subscription and group-programme charges, Mollie payment transactions and refunds, dunning state and the accounting export lines for Twinfield; the sales-ledger side of the practice administration that must satisfy the 7-year fiscal retention duty.

stores.name: Identity DB
stores.description: Identity and access schema for professionals, practice staff, HCI staff and citizens: credential hashes, two-factor secrets, UZI-pass and DigiD assertion references, roles and tenant scopes, sessions, device and push registrations; separated from clinical data so authentication can be hardened, rotated and audited independently.

stores.name: Consent Registry DB
stores.description: Registry of consents and sharing decisions: opt-in for LDF and quality-register delivery, portal and e-health terms, MedMij authorisations, family sharing grants in Quli and the processing-agreement acceptance per tenant; effective-dated so any past disclosure can be matched to the consent that allowed it.

stores.name: Audit Log Store
stores.description: Write-once, hash-chained log of every read and change of a dossier, every export, declaration release, portal access, external call and administrative action across all labels, with NEN 7513-style logging fields (who, what, when, from which context) and retention tiers per entry type; the source for patient access reports and security incident investigation.

stores.name: Clinical Document Store
stores.description: Encrypted object storage organised per tenant, patient and episode for scanned referrals, correspondence and treatment reports, dictation audio kept only until transcription is confirmed, measurement attachments, signed treatment plans, invoices and declaration PDFs, and archived dossier exports; versioned and immutable once an episode is closed, with retention labels driving 20-year and 7-year deletion.

stores.name: Care Network Message Mirror
stores.description: Mirror of referrals and secure messages exchanged with ZorgDomein, ZorgMail and hospital information systems, and of the HIS/AIS connector traffic with Pharmapartners, CGM, Sanday, HealthConnected, Bricks and Vertimart: message envelopes, delivery status, acknowledgements and errors, kept as received so a referral loop can be reconstructed.

stores.name: Quality Data Staging Zone
stores.description: Encrypted staging area for the monthly pseudonymised extracts to the Landelijke Database Fysiotherapie, Keurmerk Fysiotherapie, Qualiview and MediQuest, and for benchmark files returned by the registers; files removed on a 90-day schedule after delivery confirmation, pseudonym keys kept in the secrets vault.

stores.name: Practice Analytics Warehouse
stores.description: Analytical warehouse with per-tenant marts for practice BI (production, revenue, treatment duration, referrers, waiting times, contract utilisation) and GGZ institution reporting, plus a pseudonymised platform layer for adoption, declaration acceptance, portal activation and e-health usage that feeds team metrics and KPI pyramids; never the source of a patient-facing figure.

stores.name: Tenant Config DB
stores.description: Configuration schema for every practice, institution and label instance on the multi-tenant runtime: enabled modules and integrations, discipline and template settings, declaration parameters (AGB codes, contracts, tariff versions), branding, feature flags per label and HCI One rollout wave, and the processing-agreement status; contains no patient data.

stores.name: Migration Staging Zone
stores.description: Encrypted staging area for migration batches from acquired labels (FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, Abakus, Podofile, Edevop, FysioLogic) and from competitor systems into HCI One or CRS: source exports, mapping tables, validation reports and reconciliation counts; source files deleted after the practice signs off the migration.

stores.name: Support Desk DB
stores.description: Schema for the support desk and onboarding operations: tickets with category and priority, onboarding projects and training sessions, billing-service work queues for return messages, knowledge articles and release notes per label; references tenants and users but stores no clinical content.

stores.name: Website CMS
stores.description: Content store for the Praktijkinfo practice websites under Uw Zorg Online: page content, themes, opening hours, team pages, online booking and e-consult entry points, triage widgets, hosting and domain settings and accessibility settings; public content only, personal data limited to practice contact details.

stores.name: Secrets Vault
stores.description: Key management service holding Vecozo and UZI server certificates, ZorgDomein and ZorgMail credentials, MedMij DVZA certificates, HIS/AIS connector keys, Mollie and Twinfield API keys, partner API client secrets and the pseudonymisation keys for quality-data delivery; readable only by the integration services, rotated on schedule and revoked on partner offboarding.

stores.name: Domain Event Bus
stores.description: Message bus carrying the domain events of every asset (appointment booked, note signed, claim submitted, return message received, consent granted, programme task completed, referral received, tenant migrated) between bricks and labels, the audit log, notifications, the partner API webhooks and the warehouse, with per-topic retention and tenant-scoped payloads.
